title: A project's .decade/config.toml lays out its workspace
body:
A new workspace starts with one terminal in its directory (`Workspace::new` in `src/workspace.rs`). Jack wants a project to be able to describe its own layout.

Since this was filed, a workspace holds tabs, each its own split tree. A pane can hold several windows as pane tabs, and one pane per workspace can be marked as the agent scratch pane. `workspaces.toml` (version 2, `src/save.rs`) already records all of these for restore.

## Proposal

- A project directory may hold `.decade/config.toml`, with a version key. It describes the workspace's tabs, each with its split tree and ratios. For each pane it gives a name and either a command or a plain shell, plus an optional cwd relative to the project, optional pane tabs, whether it is pinned, and whether it is the scratch pane.
- A new workspace for that directory starts from the template. Without one it gets a single terminal.
- The template runs commands from the project directory, so decade asks before using a template it has not seen. It remembers the answer by path and content hash, so a changed file asks again.
- "Save layout as template" in the palette writes the current workspace into the project's file.

## Open

- Whether a global default template in `~/.config/decade` comes later.
- Whether the template format shares structs with `workspaces.toml`, or stays a separate, hand-written format.
